At Oakmeadow we strive to provide the highest quality care that we can, although recognise that sometimes this goes wrong. We therefore welcome complaints so that we can look at what has gone wrong, apologise as appropriate, and implement changes to avoid the same problem happening to someone else.
However, an anonymous Google review means that we cannot look into the circumstances, nor learn from it, so I would encourage you or your mother to make a complaint to the surgery by post, email or phone so we can investigate.
We are sorry that on some days it is still difficult to make an appointment, although this has improved significantly. There has been a significant increase in demand since the Covid Pandemic which has affected the whole of the NHS.
At Oakmeadow surgery, we have taken many actions to increase appointment availability.
In February 2025 Oakmeadow increased the number of GP surgeries per week by 2.
In February we provided 5,365 appointments. This equates to 628 appointments per 1,000 patients. The average for local practices was 524, and for all English practices was 487. We know that we need to do better and are continuing to monitor the situation and make improvements.
I (Dr Ingrams) was asked to move to lead Oakmeadow Surgery in 2016 as all the GPs had left except Dr P Jones, who wanted to retire soon afterwards. The practice had been unable to recruit any replacement GPs.
Since 2016 we have been able to improve Oakmeadow, adopting new ways of working, and greatly expanding our team. We now have 8 permanent GPs (5 partners and 3 employed). We have never dictated which GP a patient sees, and leave this to patient choice.  I have never been in a position to be able to provide personal care to the more than 8,500 patients we have registered, especially since I retired and returned to work only one day per week.
I am proud of the improvements that our team at Oakmeadow have made, and we will continue to adjust and improve our services for patients.
